method_note: FAST MODE stage 1. Reused facts keep original checked dates. New facts verbatim from our live weddedwonderland.com pages and official pages only. No competitor venue lists. No invented capacities, prices or perks; figures in original currency.

facts.claim: When a service has a major problem, a consumer can choose to: cancel the contract and get a refund. This may not be a full refund, as the consumer needs to pay a reasonable amount for any work done so far and as expected, or keep the contract, but pay a lower price that takes the problem into account.
facts.use_note: General consumer guarantees for services, not wedding-specific. Applies to Australian suppliers under the ACL; overseas venues may not be covered (not confirmed).

facts.claim: Businesses can't take away a consumer's right to a refund or replacement for faulty products or services. It's illegal for businesses to rely on store policies or terms and conditions which deny these rights. Consumers are not entitled to a repair, replacement or refund under the consumer guarantees if they ... simply changed their mind.
facts.use_note: Change of mind: a couple who cancels by choice relies on the venue contract terms. Supports a 'cancellation and deposit terms' column.

facts.claim: Under the Australian Consumer Law, businesses must not accept payment for products or services if: they don't intend to supply the product or service; they intend to supply different products or services from those promised; they know, or should know, that they won't be able to supply the products or services by the promised date, or within a reasonable time.

Businesses do not have to give replacement services or refunds under the consumer guarantees if the actions of a third party prevented them from supplying their services. ... In this situation, consumers' right to a refund or replacement will generally depend on the terms and conditions of the agreement for supply of the service.
facts.use_note: Supports a 'postponement and force majeure terms' row. Not legal advice; say so.

facts.claim: 'by the time catering, hire, power, staffing and wet-weather cover are priced in, the villa's freedom is usually a premium, not a saving.' Questions to ask include 'What exactly is exclusive to us: which spaces, for which hours, and who else is on the property that day?' and 'What are the noise, curfew and amplified-music rules, and are they council-imposed or negotiable?'
facts.use_note: Own venue questions; link, do not repeat wholesale. Cannibalisation check: this page already has a questions-to-ask list.

facts.claim: Ask the hotel in writing for rigging points and the weight each holds, fabric fire ratings, load-in hours, and whether an outside decorator pays a fee or works beside the in-house team.
facts.use_note: Venue questions: load-in hours, outside supplier fees.

facts.claim: Is open flame allowed, allowed only when enclosed, or not allowed at all? ... Can anything be fixed to beams, walls, the ceiling or marquee poles? ... Some hotels and country houses ban naked flame outright, so get every answer in writing before you brief the florist.
facts.use_note: Venue rules column (flame, fixings). 'Get it in writing' principle.

Use our filters to narrow by guest count and location, then enquire with 3–5 favourites to compare packages and availability.' Shortlist your favourites and send enquiries directly to confirm availability and pricing.'

facts.claim: There is generally a contract whenever a seller makes an offer and a buyer accepts it. The buyer can accept a contract: by signing a written document; by saying they accept it; through actions such as paying for a product or clicking 'I agree' on a website. ... Make sure you read and understand the terms and conditions of a contract before you accept it. If you don't understand the terms and conditions, talk to a lawyer.
facts.use_note: Modified 21 July 2026. Paying a venue deposit can itself be acceptance of the contract: supports 'compare the contract before the deposit'. Business-audience page; ACCC says it does not give legal advice.

facts.claim: Laws protect consumers and small businesses from unfair terms in standard form contracts. ... Contract terms are unfair if they: cause a significant imbalance in the rights and obligations of the parties under the contract; are not reasonably necessary to protect the legitimate interests of the party who gets an advantage from the term, and would cause financial or other harm to the other party if enforced. ... examples of terms that may be unfair, including: terms that allow one party (but not the other) to end the contract; terms that penalise one party (but not the other) for breaching or ending the contract; terms that allow one party (but not the other) to change the terms of the contract. ... The unfair contract terms law does not apply to: ... terms that set out the upfront price to be paid.
facts.use_note: Relevant to one-sided cancellation, price-change and date-change clauses in Australian venue contracts. 'Only courts can make final decisions about whether a contract term is unfair.' Changes apply to standard form contracts made or renewed on or after 9 November 2023. Do not say any specific venue term is unfair. Overseas venue contracts: not covered by this page (G-03).

facts.claim: A consumer can generally end a contract with no charge if: the business has said anything false or misleading about the goods, services, terms or conditions; a service has not met a consumer guarantee; the consumer is in a cooling-off period. ... If you have a problem with an unfair contract term, you should first try contacting the business. You can ask the business to remove or change a term you think may be unfair.
facts.use_note: Supports 'ask the venue to change a term before signing'. Cooling-off is only automatic for telemarketing or door-to-door sales per the page; do not imply venues must offer one.

facts.claim: 8. Milestone Birthdays. A milestone birthday welcomes a new decade somewhere unforgettable. It might be an intimate villa weekend for a handful of people or a celebration with everyone on the guest list. We plan the venue, the dinners and the travel for those who join you. Our travel service is the place to begin, and the plan follows from the guest list.
facts.use_note: Core brand line for the milestone birthday service. Link /celebration-ideas/celebrations-we-plan and /travel. Page meta description also says 'from proposals and engagement parties to vow renewals and milestone birthdays'.

facts.claim: Engagement parties: 'A villa terrace, a vineyard lunch and a private dining room each produce a different evening. We plan the venue, the florals, the menu and the guest travel.' Family gatherings: 'The plan favours properties and activities that suit guests of every age. We coordinate rooms, transfers and the shared moments of the trip.' How we plan: '1. A first conversation with Wedded Concierge about the occasion, the guest list and the place. 2. A venue and destination shortlist. 3. Supplier coordination, from the venue to the florist and the photographer. 4. Guest travel, covering rooms, flights and transfers. 5. The planning tools in Wonderland Studio, which keep the plan, guest list and details in one place.'
facts.use_note: Venue-type framing (villa, vineyard, private dining) and the 5-step process, worded for other celebrations; reuse as our process, not as a birthday-specific claim.

facts.claim: FAQ: 'How early should we start planning a celebration abroad? We suggest starting nine to twelve months ahead where guests are travelling, so rooms, flights and dates can be settled in good time.' 'Can Wedded Wonderland arrange travel for guests? Yes. Our travel team coordinates rooms, flights and transfers for guests.' 'Our team holds preferred-partner relationships with hotels worldwide, which can provide access to selected privileges, subject to each property's terms and eligibility'.
facts.use_note: Lead time for a birthday abroad (9 to 12 months). Keep the 'subject to each property's terms and eligibility' qualifier on privileges.

facts.claim: /travel: 'For every celebration - weddings, honeymoons and the trips in between.' 'We plan it as one connected journey rather than a stack of separate bookings, and we stay reachable while you are away.' 'Eligible stays may include daily breakfast, a hotel credit, upgrade priority and other amenities at no extra cost to you.' 'Inclusions vary by hotel, rate and dates - we confirm exactly what applies to your stay in writing before you book.' 'Group contracts work differently to individual bookings, so the perks above do not carry across automatically. We negotiate and document group terms separately, and we will be clear about what your guests receive.' 'Upgrades and extended check-in or checkout generally depend on how full the hotel is that day.'
facts.use_note: Weekend away / abroad section. Always keep 'eligible' and 'may'; perks are not guaranteed and do not carry to group room blocks.

facts.claim: /travel 'How it works': 'Step 01 Tell us about the travel. Dates, destination, guest numbers, budget and what matters most to you. Fifteen minutes is usually enough to start.' 'Step 02 We agree the scope ... If any planning fee applies, you know before we start.' 'Step 03 You receive a shortlist. Two or three options with a clear recommendation, the rate, the cancellation terms and the confirmed inclusions.' 'What we need from you: Honesty about budget, a decision timeline, and any accessibility, allergy or dietary needs in your party.' Questions include 'Is anyone travelling with accessibility, mobility, allergy or dietary needs?' and 'Is this connected to a room block, event venue or family itinerary?'
facts.use_note: Supports access-for-older-guests point (mobility needs asked up front) and the shortlist process. FAQ: 'A straightforward hotel booking usually carries no planning fee. More complex itineraries, flights or group work may carry a fee, agreed with you upfront'.

legal.summary: Major problem with a service: cancel and get a refund (less a reasonable amount for work done) or keep the contract at a lower price.
Terms cannot remove consumer guarantee rights; change of mind is not covered, so a couple's own cancellation depends on the venue contract.
Businesses must not accept payment they know they cannot supply against.
Where a third party prevents supply, refund rights generally depend on the contract terms.
Paying or clicking 'I agree' can accept a contract; read the terms first, and talk to a lawyer if unclear.

Unfair terms in standard form consumer contracts (one-sided termination, penalty or variation terms) can be void if a court finds them unfair; upfront price terms are excluded; changes from 9 November 2023.
